The picture above shows the graph of a function $y=\operatorname{cos}⁡(Bx).$ Find the value of $B.$
question.worked_solution:
In order to find the value of $B,$ we first need to find the period of the function.

From the graph, we can see that function makes a complete cycle on the interval $[0,\frac{4\pi }{5}].$ So, the period is $\frac{4\pi }{5}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14254788/assets/ea4729c43c21f5206c9abd5b756efd86707cf5420640af2f86e850eb34109824.png)

We know that for a function $y=\operatorname{cos}⁡(Bx),$ the horizontal scaling factor is $\frac{1}{B},$ and the period is multiplied by the scaling factor:

$$
\text{period}=2\pi \cdot \frac{1}{B}
$$

For our particular function, the period is $\frac{4\pi }{5},$ so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4\pi }{5} & =2\pi \cdot \frac{1}{B} \\ B & =\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
